name: Arctic Open
stakes: This week is crucial for India's shuttlers to consolidate ranking points, regain form after the Asian Games, and build momentum for the remainder of the season.
summary:
India's badminton contingent arrives in Vantaa for the Arctic Open, a Super 500 event, fresh off a demanding Asian Games campaign. While the draws are yet to be revealed, expectations will naturally fall on the shoulders of the world No. 5 men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty. They are the sole seeded Indian entry and will be looking to build on their Asian Games men's team bronze medal with a strong individual showing.

In the singles categories, PV Sindhu (world No. 11) and Lakshya Sen (world No. 14) lead the charge. Sindhu, who has been battling fatigue, will be keen to find her rhythm, while Sen aims to rebound after an early exit in the Asian Games. HS Prannoy, a key contributor to the Asian Games bronze-winning team, also features, alongside promising talents like Ayush Shetty and Malvika Bansod, who are gaining valuable Super 500 exposure. Women's doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, along with mixed doubles duo Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, will be looking to convert their Asian Games quarterfinal finishes into deeper runs here, seeking greater consistency on the international circuit.
